description: The agent's vocabulary for text-to-structure machinery — tokenization, lexical analysis, parsing algorithms, grammar formalisms, abstract syntax trees. The conceptual ground on which the substrate can build (and reason about) its own text-to-graph engine. Substantial overlap with compilers/compiler_theory but specifically oriented toward parsing AS A CAPABILITY the agent reasons about.

concepts.name: token
concepts.definition: Atomic lexical unit produced by tokenization — a word, punctuation mark, number, or operator. The input to parsing.

concepts.name: lexeme
concepts.definition: (In parsing context) The actual character sequence of a token in the source. Distinct from token type. 'foo' is the lexeme; IDENTIFIER is the type.

concepts.name: tokenization
concepts.definition: The process of splitting raw text into tokens. Handles whitespace, comments, punctuation, multi-character operators. Output is a token stream.

concepts.name: lexical_analysis
concepts.definition: Synonym for tokenization at the compiler-front-end level. The 'lexer' or 'scanner' performs this. Typically driven by regular expressions over the source language's lexical grammar.

concepts.name: parser
concepts.definition: Component that consumes a token stream and produces a tree representing the syntactic structure of the input. Driven by a grammar.

concepts.name: parse_tree
concepts.definition: A tree showing how the input derives from the grammar's start symbol via production rules. Each internal node corresponds to a nonterminal; leaves are tokens. Also called concrete syntax tree.

concepts.name: abstract_syntax_tree
concepts.definition: A tree representing the syntactic structure of the input with parse-irrelevant details (e.g., parentheses) removed. The 'AST' — the canonical structure downstream tools consume.

concepts.name: grammar
concepts.definition: Formal specification of a language's syntax — a set of production rules over terminals and nonterminals plus a designated start symbol.

concepts.name: production_rule
concepts.definition: A rewrite rule of a grammar — 'nonterminal := body'. The body is a sequence of terminals and nonterminals. Defines how the nonterminal can expand.

concepts.name: terminal
concepts.definition: A symbol of a grammar that appears in the parsed input — typically a token type. Cannot be rewritten further.

concepts.name: nonterminal
concepts.definition: A symbol of a grammar that expands via production rules. Represents a syntactic category (Expression, Statement, Phrase). Does not appear in the input.

concepts.name: context_free_grammar
concepts.definition: Grammar where each production's left side is a single nonterminal. The expansion does not depend on context. Sufficient for most programming languages and a useful approximation of natural language syntax.

concepts.name: regular_grammar
concepts.definition: Grammar generating a regular language — productions of the form A := aB or A := a. Equivalent in expressive power to finite automata; can be implemented with regex.

concepts.name: context_sensitive_grammar
concepts.definition: Grammar where productions may have non-trivial context on their left side. More expressive than CFG; less efficient to parse.

concepts.name: top_down_parsing
concepts.definition: Parsing strategy: start from the grammar's start symbol and expand productions to match the input. Includes recursive descent and LL parsers.

concepts.name: bottom_up_parsing
concepts.definition: Parsing strategy: start from the input tokens and reduce them to the start symbol via productions in reverse. Includes shift-reduce, LR parsers.

concepts.name: recursive_descent_parser
concepts.definition: A top-down parser implemented as a set of mutually recursive functions, one per nonterminal. Simple to write by hand; restricted to predictive grammars.

concepts.name: LL_parser
concepts.definition: Left-to-right, leftmost-derivation parser. LL(k) uses k tokens of lookahead. Predictive; cannot handle left recursion directly.

concepts.name: LR_parser
concepts.definition: Left-to-right, rightmost-derivation parser. Bottom-up; uses a state machine + stack. Handles a strict superset of LL grammars. Includes LALR, SLR variants.

concepts.name: PEG_parser
concepts.definition: Parsing expression grammar parser. Like CFG but with ordered alternatives — no ambiguity by construction. Implemented with packrat memoization for linear time.

concepts.name: attribute_grammar
concepts.definition: A grammar augmented with attributes attached to nonterminals + semantic actions that compute them. The output of parsing is more than the tree — it's the synthesized attributes.

concepts.name: semantic_action
concepts.definition: A code fragment attached to a production that fires when the production is reduced. Builds attributes, AST nodes, or substrate nodes.

concepts.name: ambiguity
concepts.definition: A grammar property: the same input has multiple parse trees. Pathology in language design; resolved by precedence + associativity rules, or grammar refactoring.

concepts.name: left_recursion
concepts.definition: A production where the nonterminal recurses on its leftmost position. Causes top-down parsers to loop; refactored by left-factoring or handled by LR parsers.

concepts.name: lookahead
concepts.definition: The number of tokens a parser consults beyond the current position to decide between alternatives. LL(1) uses 1 token; PEG can use unbounded lookahead via backtracking.

concepts.name: error_recovery
concepts.definition: A parser's strategy for continuing after a syntax error rather than halting. Panic-mode skips tokens; phrase-level inserts repairs.

concepts.name: tokenizer_rule
concepts.definition: An individual lexer rule mapping a regex pattern to a token type. The lexer fires the longest-matching rule at each position.

concepts.name: whitespace_handling
concepts.definition: Whether and how the tokenizer treats spaces, tabs, newlines. Most languages skip them; some (Python, Haskell) make indentation significant.

rules.name: tokenization_must_precede_parsing
if: raw text is to be parsed into structure
then: the text must first be tokenized — split into atomic lexical units
the parser consumes the token stream, not raw characters
rules.why: Mixing lexical and syntactic concerns is the classic source of parser bugs. The substrate's text-to-graph pipeline should keep them separate.

rules.name: a_grammar_specifies_the_set_of_valid_inputs
if: a parser is to be written for a language
then: a grammar must be authored specifying the language's valid syntactic forms
the grammar's class (regular, CFG, CSG, PEG) determines what parsing techniques apply
rules.why: Without a grammar, parsing is ad hoc and fragile. Substrate-grade text-to-graph extraction needs grammars.

rules.name: a_parse_tree_records_the_full_derivation_an_ast_drops_noise
if: the parser produces a tree from the input
then: the parse tree records every production application (including parentheses, separators)
an AST keeps only the syntactically significant content for downstream consumers
rules.why: Substrate-grade consumers usually want the AST, not the full derivation.

rules.name: recursive_descent_parsers_cannot_handle_left_recursion_directly
if: a top-down parser is being written for a grammar with left recursion
then: the grammar must be refactored to eliminate left recursion (left-factoring or rewriting as right recursion)
OR a different parser kind (LR, PEG with packrat) must be used
rules.why: Naive left-recursive top-down parsers loop forever; this is the single most-bitten compiler-construction issue.

rules.name: an_attribute_grammar_lets_parsing_compute_synthesized_values
if: the goal of parsing is to produce structured data, not just a tree
then: an attribute grammar with semantic actions can build the structured data during parsing
the substrate's text-to-graph adapter is naturally expressible as an attribute grammar
rules.why: Substrate-grade text-to-graph is fundamentally a transduction — input tokens → output graph nodes. Attribute grammars are the standard formalism for this transduction.

rules.name: ambiguity_in_a_grammar_must_be_resolved_before_parsing_is_deterministic
if: a grammar has multiple parse trees for some input
then: the grammar is ambiguous; the parser must choose between trees
resolution: precedence + associativity, grammar refactoring, or operator-precedence parsing
rules.why: Ambiguous grammars produce nondeterministic results; substrate-grade extraction requires determinism.

rules.name: tokenization_handles_whitespace_and_comments_so_the_parser_does_not
if: the source language has whitespace and comments that don't contribute to syntax
then: the tokenizer absorbs them — they never reach the parser
the parser sees a clean token stream
rules.why: Separation of concerns. Whitespace handling in the parser bloats it; in the tokenizer it's a tight loop.

rules.name: error_recovery_lets_a_parser_report_multiple_errors_per_run
if: a parser encounters a syntax error
then: if it halts, only one error is reported per run
if it recovers (panic-mode or phrase-level), it continues and finds further errors
rules.why: User-facing parsers need error recovery; the substrate's text-to-graph adapter benefits when ingesting noisy or partially-malformed input.
